"Humanly" means in a way that relates to human beings — specifically, within the boundaries of what human beings are capable of, or in the way that human beings naturally think, feel, and react.

Think of it this way: humans are not gods, not machines, not superheroes. We have real limits — in strength, time, knowledge, and ability. "Humanly" is the word that points to those limits. It says: "This is the world of human beings we are talking about — with everything that comes with it."

1. Within the limits of what humans can do

This is by far the most common and important use of "humanly." When you say something is "humanly possible" or "humanly impossible," you are drawing a line — the line of what any human being, no matter how talented or hardworking, can or cannot do.

  • "I did everything humanly possible to save him."

Here, the speaker is saying: I pushed myself to the absolute edge of what any human being could do. There was nothing more a person could have done.

  • "It is not humanly possible to be in two places at the same time."

No human, no matter how capable, can do this. It is beyond the reach of all humans.

  • "She worked as fast as humanly possible."

As fast as any human being is physically and mentally capable of working.

Notice that "humanly" adds emphasis and weight here. It does not just mean "possible" — it means possible for a human being, given our natural limits. It reminds you that you are talking about a real person, not a machine or a superhero.

2. From a human point of view, or as any person would naturally feel

In this second use, "humanly" describes something from the perspective of ordinary human nature — how humans naturally think, react, or feel.

  • "Humanly speaking, I completely understand why she was furious."

From a natural human standpoint, from the way any person would see it, her anger makes total sense.

  • "Humanly, it was impossible not to feel sad watching that scene."

As any normal human being would feel, sadness was unavoidable.

Here, "humanly" acts as a gentle reminder that the speaker is viewing things through the lens of human emotion and experience — not coldly, not logically, but as a real person.

These two words are very easy to confuse because they look almost identical. However, they mean completely different things.

Humanely (with an 'e') means with kindness, compassion, and mercy. It is about treating someone or something gently and with care.
"The animals were treated humanely." → with care and kindness.

Humanly (without the 'e') means within human limits, or in a human way.
"I did everything humanly possible." → to the very edge of what a person can do.

A simple way to keep them apart: "humanely" is about how kindly something is done. "Humanly" is about whether humans are even capable of doing it at all.
The Phrases You Will Most Often See

"Humanly" almost always appears alongside a small group of words. Learning these phrases will cover the vast majority of cases you'll ever encounter:

Everything humanly possible — the most common phrase in the language. It means doing the absolute maximum that any person can do.
"The doctors did everything humanly possible."

Humanly possible / humanly impossible — used to describe what is or is not within human reach.
"No single person could humanly manage all of this alone."

Humanly conceivable — within what the human mind can even imagine.
"This is the greatest kindness humanly conceivable."

Humanly speaking — used to introduce a human, personal perspective, as opposed to a strictly technical or divine one.
"Humanly speaking, the odds were completely against them."

When a speaker or writer uses "humanly," they are often doing one of two things emotionally:

They are either expressing great effort and sincerity — "I tried everything humanly possible" carries a sense of devotion, of someone who gave everything they had.

Or they are expressing humility about human limits — "It's not humanly possible" acknowledges, honestly, that we are not all-powerful. There are things beyond us.

In both cases, the word quietly reminds you: we are human, and that means something.
